subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes & $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ross <dross@acme-retail.com>, Tom Li <tli@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget range, benchmarking

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and the asks I promised to follow up on regarding pricing benchmarking:

1) Your stated volumes / usage profile (please confirm):
   - Active production usage: ~30-40M tokens / month (chat + light context)
   - Embedding batch jobs: ~10M tokens / month (monthly batched runs)
   - Peak day bursts up to ~6M tokens

2) Budget / target economics you mentioned on the call:
   - Target monthly budget range: $8k–$11k / month
   - That converts to an implied target unit cost of roughly $200–$275 per 1M tokens (please confirm we did that math right on our side)

3) What I’m sending you next:
   - A short benchmarking summary vs. public list prices for OpenAI/Anthropic and typical hosted open-model providers (attached: Redwood_Pricing_Benchmark_1M_tokens_v1.pdf)
   - A straw mutual action plan (attached) that maps milestones and procurement steps

High-level takeaways I want to call out:
- If your target is ~ $200–$275 / 1M tokens, we can show a path to that number for higher-cost models by combining Redwood routing + caching + model-variant fallbacks, but the biggest wins come from moving to an open-model variant for production traffic.
- Broad benchmarking ranges (by model class):
   * OpenAI (managed): ~ $80–$300 / 1M tokens depending on model (older text/codex vs newer multi-turn models).
   * Anthropic (managed): ~ $70–$260 / 1M tokens depending on model and context length.
   * Hosted open-models (quantized, self-hosted or managed hosts): ~ $15–$90 / 1M tokens depending on quantization & infra efficiency.

Ask / next step: Can you confirm the 30–40M tokens / month figure and the $8k–$11k budget range? If confirmed, I’ll schedule a short pricing call next week to go through an ACME-specific unit economics model and a draft commercial term (including first-year incentives).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Benchmark_1M_tokens_v1.pdf
From: Danielle Ross <dross@acme-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tli@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget range, benchmarking

Thanks Vanessa — yes this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed volumes: ~35M tokens/month steady-state (chat + short context), plus ~12M tokens/month for embeddings/batch jobs. So total ~47M tokens/month.
- Budget: target monthly spend is firming up around $9k–$11k. We’re trying to hit <= $240 / 1M tokens as a target for overall average across both chat and embedding workloads.
- Important: we have a hard preference that any move to open models preserves parity on latency for peak bursts — we’ll need the Dedicated/Private options scoped if the unit economics look right.

Can you include a simple per-1M comparison vs OpenAI and Anthropic (list price) and an example Redwood blended price if we route chat to an open-model variant + keep fallback to OpenAI for the highest-quality flows?

Appreciate it — Danielle
Danielle Ross
Head of AI Products | Acme Retail
+dross@acme-retail.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ross <dross@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tli@acme-retail.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget range, benchmarking

Thanks for confirming, Danielle — really helpful. Attached is the short benchmarking deck I mentioned and a quick-blended example below for the ~47M token profile you shared.

Benchmarks (public list / typical ranges) — per 1M tokens (approx):
- OpenAI managed (mix of cheaper & higher-quality endpoints): $90 – $300 / 1M tokens
- Anthropic managed (mix): $80 – $260 / 1M tokens
- Typical hosted open-model providers / self-hosted (quantized + infra optimized): $15 – $90 / 1M tokens

ACME blended example (illustrative):
- Profile: 35M chat tokens (most latency-sensitive), 12M embedding tokens (batch)
- Option A (fallback-heavy, managed-first): 100% managed (OpenAI/Anthropic): assume blended $200 / 1M -> monthly spend ~ $9,400
- Option B (Redwood routing + open-model primary): route 75% chat to open-model variant (lower cost), keep 25% chat on managed for highest-quality. Embeddings on open hosts. Assumed blended costs: open-model $40 / 1M, managed $220 / 1M -> blended ~ $95 / 1M -> monthly spend ~ $4,465

Bottom line: For your target (~$240 / 1M target), Option A meets it but offers limited upside. Option B shows a ~50%+ cost reduction, which would get you well below the $240 target and leave room for commercial incentives/discounting while still giving you managed fallbacks during peak/critical flows.

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 30-minute pricing walkthrough next Tue/Wed to go through the blended P&L model (I’ll bring a simple spreadsheet)
- I’ll loop in Marissa (rev ops) and Aditya (solutions) to propose a first-year incentive (volume commit or reserved capacity) and a draft term sheet

Sharing attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Benchmark_1M_tokens_v1.pdf; Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:35:00 +0000
Subject: [Internal] ACME pricing — need commercial latitude for blended routing approach

Team — forwarding Acme thread. They confirmed ~47M tokens/month and want target ~<= $240 / 1M. I ran a quick blended scenario and Option B (open-model primary with managed fallback) gets us to ~ $95 / 1M blended for their profile. That gives us room for commercial concession while protecting margin.

Can we do the following:
- Marissa: will RevOps allow a first-year incentive of 20% off list for the first 12 months if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (Dedicated burst + private onboarding optional)?
- Aditya: can Solutions guarantee we can support the latency SLO for 75% open-model traffic + 25% managed fallback for peaks? If we need Dedicated pools, we should flag capacity/lead time.

I attached the mutual action plan and the benchmark PDF. Planning to set a 30-min pricing walkthrough with Acme for Tue 24 Mar. Please reply with yes/no and any constraints.

Thanks,
Vanessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Internal] ACME pricing — need commercial latitude for blended routing approach

Vanessa — sounds reasonable. We can offer a first-year 20% customer incentive off our proposed blended commercial rate tied to a 12-month commit (we'd use a reserved capacity clause to protect throughput). A few notes:
- Bookings team needs expected ARR / committed monthly spend to size discount properly — use the blended monthly example ($4.5k/mo) as the baseline and include a minimum commit (e.g., $3.5k/mo)
- Legal will want standard T&Cs + SLA for Dedicated/PV options; procurement lead time ~4–6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning in our typical regions

Aditya — please confirm feasibility of the routing + latency SLO and any Dedicated lead time we should tell the customer.

-M
